findings.title: c7db4e5's own itemized claim omits two of its own files
findings.before: templates/README.md: "One exception: `queue-guard.sh.tmpl` is copied byte-for-byte from PF's Stop hook and carries no header, so the upstream text stays comparable; the sidecar hash is what marks it managed." / docs/src/guide/install.md had no consumer gloss at all.
findings.after: templates/README.md: "Two exceptions: `queue-guard.sh.tmpl`...; and `SKILL.md.tmpl` carries the ordinary Markdown header but NOT on the first line — it follows the mandatory YAML frontmatter..." / install.md gains: "A **consumer** is a package that pins this tool and is reviewed by it — one of the four GBG science packages, or the tool itself, which is its own fifth consumer."
findings.why_it_matters: The commit's own message partitions its 25 named edits into exactly four buckets (RATIONALE 8, SRC 7, SCRIPTS 6, REGISTERS 4) and states the pass closed 28 of 37 banked findings "by class, not by line" — a precise, auditable accounting. Neither of these two real, substantive file edits is named anywhere in that accounting; templates/README.md is not mentioned in this commit's message or any later one in the range, and install.md's gloss surfaces only two commits later (36788aa), described in the past tense as something "I glossed... at its first use in install.md" without ever being credited in c7db4e5 itself. In an instrument whose entire design point is that self-certifying commit messages are claims and not evidence, a commit that enumerates its own scope and then silently exceeds it by two files is exactly the failure mode this lane exists to catch — even though both edits are, on their merits, legitimate and narrow.
findings.description: The fix-pass commit c7db4e5 presents itself as a complete, categorised inventory of what it fixed (RATIONALE/SRC/SCRIPTS/REGISTERS, 8+7+6+4=25 items covering 28 of 37 findings), but its actual diff touches two files — templates/README.md and docs/src/guide/install.md — that appear in none of the four paragraphs. Both edits are individually sound (verified against the current templates/SKILL.md.tmpl file and the install.md @ref target), so this is not a behaviour or contract defect; it is a gap between what the commit claims to account for and what it actually changed, the specific shape this lane is built to surface.
findings.evidence: c7db4e5 diffstat lists `templates/README.md | 8 ++++---` and `docs/src/guide/install.md | 2 ++` among its 18 changed files, but grepping the full commit message body for "template", "README", "install.md" or "consumer" finds no match; the only later trace is 36788aa's message: "pages#2: I glossed \"consumer\" at its first use in install.md and left the bare uses..." — crediting the fix to a different commit's retrospective, not to c7db4e5 itself.
